# `unconsumed-delimiter`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a loop that reads with `takeDelimiterExclusive` but never consumes the
delimiter, so every later iteration reads an empty slice.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`std.Io.Reader.takeDelimiterExclusive` returns the bytes before the delimiter
and advances up to it, not past it. The delimiter stays buffered, so the next
call returns an empty slice, and so does every call after that: a `while` loop
reading lines this way spins forever after the first line, and a counted loop
reads empty records.

## When it fires

It reports a `takeDelimiterExclusive` call inside a `while` or `for` loop, or
in a `while` condition, when the loop does nothing else with the reader. Any
other method call on the reader (`toss(1)`, `discardDelimiterInclusive`,
`takeByte`, a peek), a method call on an object that holds it, or passing the
reader on keeps the loop quiet. Use `takeDelimiter`, which consumes the
delimiter and returns `null` at the end of the stream, or call `toss(1)` after
each line.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn countLines(reader: *std.Io.Reader) usize {
    var count: usize = 0;
    while (reader.takeDelimiterExclusive('\n')) |_| {
        count += 1;
    } else |_| {}
    return count;
}
```
